reviewed_by: Claude review of the Ask Nebula popup WebKit flake
reason: SelectionActionsProvider ends a selected-text action with a 180ms exit that called document.getSelection().removeAllRanges(). Ask Nebula focuses its question box before the exit finishes, so the selection being cleared is that box's caret; WebKit then keeps focus on the box but drops every keystroke until it is clicked (3/3 in Playwright's WebKit, Chromium kept the text). The exit now leaves the selection alone when the action moved focus into a text box, and still clears it when focus stayed put. selectionActions.test.tsx covers both paths and fails on the old provider. The same race caused the popup e2e's toHaveValue flake (fill's insertText landing after the caret was cleared) and a 30s timeout when the second popup's fill lost its text and Ask question stayed disabled. The e2e now types into the auto-focused box after the toolbar has gone, which fails every run on WebKit without the fix. The mobile-webkit CI failure in run 35597735135 was not a timeout: its traces show the page closing about 5s into the test, and locally the WPEWebProcess core shows a SIGSEGV on a WebKit RunLoop thread. Drag loops crashed it within 20 drags every time (launcher 3/3, launcher without pointer capture 2/2, popup handle 2/2), while keyboard loops, a plain page drag and a tap never did, so WebKit projects move the launcher and popup with the keyboard and Chromium projects keep the pointer drags. The assistant entries on mobile-webkit and mobile-chromium run the popup test and both selected-context tests that go through the toolbar.
exclusions: Full Python, frontend and Playwright suites are excluded. No Python or native code changed. The assistant/desktop entry and the ask-nebula-popup area on its other six projects are not selected: locally the desktop assistant entry passed (52 passed, 1 existing skip) and the popup test passed 3/3 on compact, mobile-chromium-small, mobile-chromium-wide, mobile-chromium-ledger-390, mobile-webkit-small and mobile-webkit-wide. The popup test also passed with --repeat-each 10 on mobile-webkit and mobile-chromium, and the selected entries passed in full locally (mobile-webkit 48, mobile-chromium 45 plus 4 existing skips). The real-Core journeys that use the selection toolbar are not selected: the provider change only skips clearing a selection that a newly focused text box owns, which the unit test covers. AskNebulaPopup.test.tsx and the WorkbenchDraftContext tests were run locally and pass; neither file changed.
